description: Consonant sound records keyed by the 27 shared letter ids. changesSound marks the letters whose sound depends on dagesh/dots/tradition. verified=false records are standard values that were NOT in the fetched side-by-side table. say = one plain beginner sentence per tradition (<=15 words, no IPA), shown on first-day and lesson screens; unreviewed by a native speaker.

alef.name: Alef

english.israeli: silent / a glottal stop between vowels (uh-oh)
english.sephardi: silent / a glottal stop between vowels (uh-oh)
english.american_synagogue: silent / a glottal stop between vowels (uh-oh)

say.israeli: Alef says nothing; it holds a vowel, like the catch in uh-oh.
say.sephardi: Alef says nothing; it holds a vowel, like the catch in uh-oh.
say.ashkenazi: Alef says nothing; it only holds a vowel.

alef.notes: Ashkenazi alef is silent at all times in most forms.

bet.name: Bet / Vet

say.israeli: Bet says B, like the b in ball; no dot, V as in vine.
say.sephardi: Bet says B, like the b in ball; no dot, V as in vine.
say.ashkenazi: Bet says B, like the b in ball; no dot, V as in vine.

bet.notes: One of the three letters that still alternate in Modern Hebrew.

gimel.name: Gimel

english.israeli: hard g as in game, never soft
english.sephardi: hard g as in game, never soft
english.ashkenazi: hard g as in game, never soft
english.american_synagogue: hard g as in game, never soft

say.israeli: Gimel says G, like the g in grumpy, never like gem.
say.sephardi: Gimel says G, like the g in grumpy, never like gem.
say.ashkenazi: Gimel says G, like the g in grumpy, never like gem.

gimel.notes: No alternation in Modern Hebrew. Jewfaq: always a hard g.

say.israeli: Dalet says D, like the d in dive.
say.sephardi: Dalet says D, like the d in dive.
say.ashkenazi: Dalet says D, like the d in dive.

he.name: He

english.israeli: h; silent at the end of a word unless it has mappiq
english.sephardi: h; silent at the end of a word unless it has mappiq
english.ashkenazi: h; silent at the end of a word unless it has mappiq
english.american_synagogue: h; silent at the end of a word unless it has mappiq

say.israeli: He says H, like the h in hey; usually silent ending a word.
say.sephardi: He says H, like the h in hey; usually silent ending a word.
say.ashkenazi: He says H, like the h in hey; usually silent ending a word.

he.notes: Final he without mappiq is a vowel letter. Fast-speech he-dropping is unsourced (see drills TODO).

vav.name: Vav

english.israeli: v; also the vowel letter for o (cholam malei) and u (shuruk)
english.sephardi: v; also the vowel letter for o (cholam malei) and u (shuruk)
english.ashkenazi: v; also the vowel letter for o (cholam malei) and u (shuruk)
english.american_synagogue: v; also the vowel letter for o (cholam malei) and u (shuruk)

say.israeli: Vav says V, like the v in vine; it can also be O or U.
say.sephardi: Vav says V, like the v in vine; it can also be O or U.
say.ashkenazi: Vav says V, like the v in vine; it can also be O or U.

vav.notes: As a vowel letter see the cholam/shuruk records.

zayin.name: Zayin

say.israeli: Zayin says Z, like the z in zipper.
say.sephardi: Zayin says Z, like the z in zipper.
say.ashkenazi: Zayin says Z, like the z in zipper.

zayin.notes: Not in the fetched side-by-side table; standard value, lane-3 inference. Check with a native speaker or phonetics reference.

chet.name: Chet

english.israeli: ch as in Bach / loch (back-of-throat, no English chair sound)
english.sephardi: pharyngeal [ħ], a throat sound (the ch of Bach / loch is the Israeli merged value)
english.ashkenazi: ch as in Bach / loch (back-of-throat, no English chair sound); the pharyngeal is seldom observed in practice

say.israeli: Chet says CH, like the ch in Bach: clear your throat softly.
say.sephardi: Chet says CH, like the ch in Bach, but deeper in the throat.
say.ashkenazi: Chet says CH, like the ch in Bach: clear your throat softly.

chet.notes: General Israeli: chet and khaf merged into one sound. Older Mizrahi speakers keep the pharyngeal. Strict liturgical usage asks for the pharyngeal but it is rarely observed. The per-tradition English lines follow the stored IPA; needs-native-review.

tet.name: Tet

say.israeli: Tet says T, like the t in tea; Tav sounds the same.
say.sephardi: Tet says T, like the t in tea; Tav sounds the same.
say.ashkenazi: Tet says T, like the t in tea.

tet.notes: General Israeli lost the emphatic sounds of Biblical Hebrew (Wikipedia). Which Sephardi/Mizrahi communities keep emphatic tet was not in our sources.

yod.name: Yod

english.israeli: y as in yes; vowel letter for i/ei
english.sephardi: y as in yes; vowel letter for i/ei
english.ashkenazi: y as in yes; vowel letter for i/ei
english.american_synagogue: y as in yes; vowel letter for i/ei

say.israeli: Yod says Y, like the y in yo-yo.
say.sephardi: Yod says Y, like the y in yo-yo.
say.ashkenazi: Yod says Y, like the y in yo-yo.

yod.notes: Not in the fetched side-by-side table; standard value, lane-3 inference. Check with a native speaker or phonetics reference.

kaf.name: Kaf / Khaf

say.israeli: Kaf says K, like the k in kernel; no dot, clear your throat softly (ch).
say.sephardi: Kaf says K, like the k in kernel; no dot, clear your throat softly (ch).
say.ashkenazi: Kaf says K, like the k in kernel; no dot, clear your throat softly (ch).

kaf.notes: Khaf is the same sound as chet in General Israeli.

kaf-final.name: Final kaf

say.israeli: Final Kaf says CH, like clearing your throat softly.
say.sephardi: Final Kaf says CH, like clearing your throat softly.
say.ashkenazi: Final Kaf says CH, like clearing your throat softly.

kaf-final.notes: Same sounds as kaf; the Priestly Blessing ends one word with ךָּ (dagesh) so it is read k.

lamed.name: Lamed

say.israeli: Lamed says L, like the l in lamp.
say.sephardi: Lamed says L, like the l in lamp.
say.ashkenazi: Lamed says L, like the l in lamp.

lamed.notes: Not in the fetched side-by-side table; standard value, lane-3 inference. Check with a native speaker or phonetics reference.

mem.name: Mem

say.israeli: Mem says M, like the m in mom.
say.sephardi: Mem says M, like the m in mom.
say.ashkenazi: Mem says M, like the m in mom.

mem.notes: Not in the fetched side-by-side table; standard value, lane-3 inference. Check with a native speaker or phonetics reference.

nun.name: Nun

say.israeli: Nun says N, like the n in nap.
say.sephardi: Nun says N, like the n in nap.
say.ashkenazi: Nun says N, like the n in nap.

nun.notes: Not in the fetched side-by-side table; standard value, lane-3 inference. Check with a native speaker or phonetics reference.

samekh.name: Samekh

say.israeli: Samekh says S, like the s in sit.
say.sephardi: Samekh says S, like the s in sit.
say.ashkenazi: Samekh says S, like the s in sit.

samekh.notes: Chabad notes Ashkenazim read an unaccented tav like samekh (see tav).

sources.label: Chabad: The Difference Between Sepharadic and Ashkenazic Pronunciation

ayin.name: Ayin

english.israeli: silent / glottal stop; do not try a pharyngeal in Israel
english.sephardi: pharyngeal [ʕ] (Western Sephardim [ŋ]); silent in Israeli and Ashkenazi

say.israeli: Ayin says nothing, like Alef; it only holds a vowel.
say.sephardi: Ayin says a squeezed throat sound; Israeli Hebrew keeps it silent.
say.ashkenazi: Ayin says nothing, like Alef; it only holds a vowel.

ayin.notes: General Israeli ayin is absorbed by alef. A pharyngeal learned in shul can mark a speaker as an outsider in Israel. The per-tradition English lines follow the stored IPA; needs-native-review.

pe.name: Pe / Fe

say.israeli: Pe says P, like the p in pop; no dot, F as in fluff.
say.sephardi: Pe says P, like the p in pop; no dot, F as in fluff.
say.ashkenazi: Pe says P, like the p in pop; no dot, F as in fluff.

pe.notes: Aspiration of p/t/k compared with English is unsourced (see drills).

say.israeli: Tsadi says TS, like the ts in pizza: a T sliding into S.
say.sephardi: Tsadi says TS, like the ts in pizza: a T sliding into S.
say.ashkenazi: Tsadi says TS, like the ts in pizza: a T sliding into S.

say.israeli: Qof says K, like the k in kite: back of tongue lifts to the roof.
say.sephardi: Qof says K, like the k in kite: back of tongue lifts to the roof.
say.ashkenazi: Qof says K, like the k in kite: back of tongue lifts to the roof.

resh.name: Resh

ipa.sephardi: alveolar trill or tap (like Spanish r)
ipa.ashkenazi: alveolar or uvular, by regional dialect

english.israeli: back-of-the-throat r (like French or German r), not the English r
english.sephardi: front r, rolled or tapped (like Spanish r)
english.ashkenazi: r varies by regional dialect: front (alveolar) or back-of-the-throat (uvular)
english.american_synagogue: most Americans say English r as in rail

say.israeli: Resh says R, like French r: at the back of your throat, not the tongue.
say.sephardi: Resh says R, like Spanish r: tap your tongue tip behind your top teeth.
say.ashkenazi: Resh says R: tongue tip or back of the throat, depending on your dialect.

resh.notes: Nearly all Israeli Jews use a uvular resh. Using the English [ɹ] is a leading outsider marker. The Sephardi and Ashkenazi English lines follow the stored IPA; needs-native-review.

shin.name: Shin / Sin

ipa.israeli: [ʃ] with right dot, [s] with left dot

english.israeli: sh with the right dot, s with the left dot
english.sephardi: sh with the right dot, s with the left dot
english.ashkenazi: sh with the right dot, s with the left dot
english.american_synagogue: sh with the right dot, s with the left dot

say.israeli: Shin says SH, like shh; left dot, S as in sit.
say.sephardi: Shin says SH, like shh; left dot, S as in sit.
say.ashkenazi: Shin says SH, like shh; left dot, S as in sit.

shin.notes: Lithuanian Ashkenazi historically merged both as [s] (historical).

tav.name: Tav

english.ashkenazi: s without dagesh (Shabbos), t with dagesh
english.american_synagogue: t in prayer; s in Orthodox shuls and in English loanwords such as Shabbos

say.israeli: Tav says T, like the t in table; Tet sounds the same.
say.sephardi: Tav says T, like the t in table; Tet sounds the same.
say.ashkenazi: Tav says S, a hiss, like the s in Shabbos; with a dot, T.

tav.notes: The single most audible Ashkenazi/Sephardi switch (Yit-gadal vs Yis-gadal).

features.summary: Bet is b with dagesh and v without.
Kaf is k with dagesh and kh (like loch) without.
Pe is p with dagesh and f without.
The dot decides: right dot = sh, left dot = s.
Dagesh kal hardens begadkefat letters (only bet, kaf, pe change sound in Israeli Hebrew). Dagesh chazak (doubling) is not pronounced in Modern Hebrew.
In General Israeli chet and khaf are one sound [χ]; older Mizrahi speakers keep the pharyngeal chet.
In General Israeli ayin is merged with alef. Pharyngeal ayin survives in Sephardi/Mizrahi tradition; Ashkenazi is silent.
Nearly all Israeli Jews pronounce resh as a uvular fricative; the English r is the typical American carry-over.
Ashkenazi tav without dagesh is s (Shabbos); Sephardi and Israeli tav is always t.
